claims.text: Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi in a simple solid-solution state has low hardness and strength because strong dislocation obstacles are absent.
Ordered precipitates and significant short-range ordering would act as strong obstacles to dislocation motion in CoCrFeNiTi.
The absence of such obstacles permits relatively easy dislocation glide and plastic flow.
Deformation of the simple solid solution will be dominated by relatively uniform dislocation slip.
The simple solid solution will show little dislocation accumulation and few secondary phases capable of pinning dislocations.
Easy dislocation glide explains the combination of good ductility and machinability with limited strength and hardness.
The applicable starting material is arc-melted, near-equimolar CoCrFeNiTi that is solution annealed into a single-phase solid solution and is not aged.
The as-synthesized state lacks significant short-range ordering, long-range ordering, and precipitation particles.
CoCrFeNiTi has a moderate stacking-fault energy that facilitates cross-slip.
Cross-slip reduces dislocation interactions and accumulation that would otherwise raise strength.
Relative to an aged or short-range-ordered CoCrFeNiTi control, the simple solid solution will exhibit fewer dislocation pile-ups.
Relative to the aged or ordered control, the simple solid solution will exhibit fewer dislocation-forest interactions.
Relative to the aged or ordered control, the simple solid solution will have lower strength and hardness.
Relative to the aged or ordered control, the simple solid solution will have higher tensile ductility.
The proposed mechanism applies from room temperature to about 600 °C and at strain rates up to about 10^-3 s^-1.
Formation of additional phases or ordering outside the stated boundary may change the operative deformation mechanisms.
Solid-solution and stacking-fault-energy effects are relevant to strength and deformation in high-entropy alloys generally.
The stacking-fault energy and degree of short-range ordering in CoCrFeNiTi have not been directly measured.
Aging the same CoCrFeNiTi composition can produce fine precipitates or short-range ordering suitable for a controlled comparison.
